rationale: Submit a successor of the startup-replay experiment that tests the batch-capacity boundary at MaxAppendEntries=1024 with 131072 entries (128 batches) and 131073 entries (129 batches). Native feedback showed the 128-batch case returning in 45 ms while the 129-batch case did not return in five seconds, so the retained receipt should show the boundary follows the batch count rather than the default entry count.

scope.description: Five restart attempts with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled: a commit-tracking store seeded with 8192 committed command entries (exactly 128 batches at MaxAppendEntries=64), the same seeded store with 8193 entries (129 batches), the same 8193 entries with MaxAppendEntries=1024 (9 batches), and two restarts of retained state produced by a real single-node cluster that committed 8300 commands through the normal leader/commit/apply path, one after an explicit Snapshot() and one without a snapshot. Two further seeded cases replay 131072 and 131073 committed entries with MaxAppendEntries=1024, which correspond to 128 and 129 batches.
assumptions: The FSM batch channel capacity (128) is a constant of the captured code; MaxAppendEntries is a validated configuration field and is recorded per case.
Each case builds its own stores and transport, so cases do not share state; the real-prefix cases reuse exactly the stores written by the producing raft.
NewRaft is invoked on its own goroutine and observed for a bounded window; a case that never returns is reported as returned=false rather than as a harness failure.
fsm_applied_sampled is a single observation at the end of the window, not a completion marker.
excluded: No assertions about commit safety, voting or membership; this probe addresses startup progress only.

Replay lengths produced by shortening a real-prefix snapshot partially (between 1 and 128 batches) are still not exercised; only the seeded 9-batch case and the 0-batch snapshot control bracket that region.

experiment.prefix: Per case the harness creates an InmemCommitTrackingStore (and InmemSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, assuranceFSM) and emits startup_case_<case> with the configured MaxAppendEntries, staged commit index, last log index, snapshot index and derived replay batch count. Seeded cases store LogCommand entries 1..N and stage commit index N; control_same_entries_larger_batches seeds the same 8193 entries as trigger_129_batches but builds its Config with MaxAppendEntries=1024. Real-prefix cases call BootstrapCluster for a single voter, start the producing raft with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, wait for leadership, apply 8300 commands through Apply futures on the leader, optionally call Snapshot(), then Shutdown(). The restart then calls NewRaft with a fresh Config (RestoreCommittedLogs=true), a fresh FSM and a fresh transport on the retained stores, bounded by the case timeout; startup_result_<case> records returned, elapsed_ms, error, sampled FSM apply count and the number of newly blocked processLogs/restoreFromCommittedLogs goroutines relative to a pre-case stack sample. The two added cases seed 131072 and 131073 committed command entries and restart with MaxAppendEntries=1024; their case events record the derived batch count and the result events record whether NewRaft returned.
semantic_changes: Two cases exercise the same batch-capacity boundary at MaxAppendEntries=1024: 131072 entries (128 batches) and 131073 entries (129 batches).
Two comparisons assert that the larger-batch replay completes at 128 batches and at 129 batches.
experiment.responsibility: The library, not the caller, owns the size and lifetime of its FSM dispatch channel: it chooses the batch size, creates fsmMutateCh, and decides the order in which NewRaft starts the FSM consumer. The documented RestoreCommittedLogs option promises to replay all known-committed logs on disk before completing NewRaft, so it must complete for a legal (store, commit index) state rather than block the caller that cannot yet shut it down.

comparisons.description: Exactly 128 replay batches (the channel capacity) must still let NewRaft complete.
A real-prefix restart whose snapshot bounds the replay must let NewRaft complete.
The same 8193 committed entries replayed as 9 batches must let NewRaft complete; a failure here would attribute the block to entry count rather than batch count.
One entry past the 128-batch capacity must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.
A real cluster restart with 130 replay batches must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.
Exactly 128 batches at MaxAppendEntries=1024 must let NewRaft complete.
One entry past the same 128-batch capacity at MaxAppendEntries=1024 must also complete; a false witness contradicts it.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds two cases at MaxAppendEntries=1024 that place the replay exactly at and one entry past the 128-batch capacity derived from the fixed channel size, so the boundary can be checked at an entry count far from the default configuration. Existing cases and comparisons are unchanged.
